question.text: What is 'option assignment' and when does it occur?

answer.text: Assignment is the process where an option seller is notified that the option buyer has exercised their right — the seller must fulfill the obligation to buy (put) or sell (call) the underlying. In Indian exchange-traded options (European), assignment only occurs at expiry
Assignment is the process of allocating a new option contract to a market maker
Assignment can happen at any time for any option type in India
Assignment only applies to the option buyer, not the seller

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series VIII page 61 explains the obligations of an option writer and defines assignment as the allocation of exercised options to sellers. Page 63 confirms that for exchange-traded index and stock options in India, exercise and assignment are permitted only on the expiration date. Series I page 90 and Series XVI page 66 mirror this European-only rule for currency and commodity options respectively. The Trap: Assignment is not the allocation of new contracts to a market maker, and it is not a buyer-side activity — the buyer exercises and the seller is assigned. American-style early assignment does not apply in India because all listed equity, currency and commodity options are European. Note: Detailed allocation mechanics (random/proportional) are not covered in the pages checked; the answer is restricted to the supported exercise, assignment and European-expiry logic from VIII pp.61 & 63, I p.90 and XVI p.66.
